title: Protocol optimization for simultaneous DNA and RNA co-extraction from single hard tick specimens
author: Cafiso, Chiappa, et al.
materials: The quantification of the extracted DNA and RNA samples was performed using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Qubit RNA Broad-Range Assay Kit and Qubit DNA Broad-Range Assay Kit; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc., Carlsbad, CA, USA), the purity was evaluated using a spectrophotometer (Nanodrop ND-1000 Spectrophotometer; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) and the integrity was determined using Agilent TapeStation 2200 (Agilent, Santa Clara, CA, USA). Information about nucleic acid concentration (ng/µl), and 260/280 and 260/230 ratios values are shown in Table 1. In addition, the integrity of the extracted RNA, which is pivotal for possible subsequent gene expression and/or transcriptomic analyses, is indicated as RNA integrity number (RIN). The median of the RIN values was 8.95, which suggests a good integrity of the RNA, since a RIN of 10 represents highly intact RNA (electropherograms are shown in Supplementary Fig. 1).Table 1Data obtained on unengorged and semi-engorged tick specimens tested for the protocol optimization after: (i) RNA extraction of 19 samples using TRIzolⓇ LS Reagent, (ii) DNA extraction of 13 samples following TRIzolⓇ LS Reagent manufacturer's protocol and (ii) DNA extraction of six samples using a commercial kit (NucleoSpinⓇ Tissue kit, Macherey-Nagel, Düren, Germany). RNA and DNA yield variabilities were observed, probably due to different tick engorgement phases (Table 1). In fact, nucleic acids belonging to the arthropod, vertebrate host's blood and tick microbial community can affect the total amount of the extracted genetic material. Furthermore, when compared, extraction results obtained by isolating DNA using TRIzolⓇ LS protocol and the commercial kit showed similar DNA concentrations (ng/µl) as well as similar 260/280 ratio (p > 0.05 for both). However, lower 260/230 ratio values were observed for those samples extracted using TRIzolⓇ LS compared to the commercial kit (p = 0.027). This difference is probably related to the higher efficiency of the kit-based isolation in removing contaminants, such as phenol, that can decrease 260/230 ratio values. Finally, nucleic acids yield variability did not affect the PCR results for any of the extracted sample (as indicated in ‘PCR validation on DNA and cDNA samples’ section).

cDNA was synthetized starting from 800 ng of total RNA using the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany), with genomic DNA (gDNA) removal step carried out following manufacturer's instructions. In fact, the presence of contaminant DNA in some of the isolated RNA samples was confirmed through RNA quantification before and after DNase treatment (5–10% of DNA contamination; RNase-Free DNase set, Qiagen, Hilden, Germany). gDNA-removal step is pivotal in case of transcriptomics and gene expression analyses, but can be surely avoided in case of studies aimed at the detection of viral RNA.

steps.title: Collect and wash tick specimens
steps.instruction: Collect 11 Ixodes ricinus and 8 Hyalomma spp. adult females (14 semi‑engorged: 5 I. ricinus, 8 Hyalomma; 5 unengorged I. ricinus) in 2018, store alive in 50 ml conical tubes, transport to the lab and process the same day; wash each tick in 1 X PBS, dry on paper towels, identify under a stereomicroscope, and keep the specimens on ice in a chemical fume‑hood.

steps.title: Homogenize tick in TRIzol LS
steps.instruction: Place a single tick in a sterile RNase‑/DNase‑free 1.5 ml polypropylene tube, add 500 µl TRIzol LS, cut the tick with a sterile scalpel (blade size 11), crush with a sterile pestle, then add a further 500 µl TRIzol LS and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Freeze and ship samples
steps.instruction: Seal the tube and store at –20 °C (stopping point) until shipment; ship the frozen tubes under controlled temperature to a second laboratory.

steps.title: Thaw and separate phases
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen tubes, then add chloroform at a TRIzol LS : chloroform ratio of 3 : 1 (manufacturer’s instructions) in a chemical fume‑hood; vortex and centrifuge as recommended to separate aqueous, interphase and organic phases.

steps.title: Isolate RNA from aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Recover the aqueous phase and follow the TRIzol LS RNA isolation protocol; finally resuspend the RNA pellet in 40 µl RNase‑free water and incubate at 56 °C for 10 min to ensure complete resolubilisation, then store the RNA at –80 °C.

steps.title: Isolate DNA from interphase/organic phase (TRIzol LS method)
steps.instruction: Process the interphase/organic phase from 13 samples according to the TRIzol LS DNA isolation steps; resuspend the DNA pellet in 50 µl 1 X TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0); pellet insoluble material by centrifugation for 10 min at 12 000 × g at 4 °C, transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 ml tube and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Isolate DNA from interphase/organic phase (kit method)
steps.instruction: For six remaining samples, treat the interphase/organic phase following TRIzol LS steps 1a‑1f, precipitate DNA with 100 % ethanol, resuspend the pellet in 180 µl Buffer T1 (NucleoSpin Tissue kit), then perform DNA purification according to the NucleoSpin Tissue kit protocol; elute DNA with 50 µl 70 °C pre‑warmed Buffer BE and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify and assess nucleic acid quality
steps.instruction: Measure DNA and RNA concentrations with a Qubit 3.0 fluorometer using the RNA Broad‑Range and DNA Broad‑Range assay kits; evaluate purity with a Nanodrop ND‑1000 (record 260/280 and 260/230 ratios); determine integrity on an Agilent TapeStation 2200 and record the RNA Integrity Number (median RIN = 8.95).

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from RNA
steps.instruction: Take 800 ng of total RNA and use the QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit (Qiagen) with the included genomic DNA removal step (RNase‑Free DNase set, Qiagen); confirm DNA contamination (5–10 %) by quantifying RNA before and after DNase treatment; perform reverse transcription at 42 °C for 20 min using the RT Primer Mix (random primers + oligo‑dT); include a no‑reverse‑transcriptase control for each sample.

description: Here we describe a method for the co-extraction of DNA and RNA form single adult unengorged and semi-engorged tick specimens using TRIzolⓇ LS Reagent (Invitrogen, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., Waltham, MA, USA; hereafter “TRIzolⓇ LS”). This method permits optimal DNA and RNA co-extraction, with the use of a moderately low-cost reagent, allowing a safe handling of the samples, especially when working with low-level containment (biosafety level-2). The current method is suitable for multiple molecular analyses, in particular epidemiological studies aimed at investigating the presence of DNA- and RNA-based tick-borne pathogens (TBPs) in the same sample. Moreover, it is applicable to transcriptomics and gene expression analyses on ticks and their microbial communities, and supports studies aimed at understanding the tick metabolism and biological interactions between ticks and their symbionts, or between ticks and tick-borne pathogens, or both.
